text: Mood and anxiety disorders are the most common pregnancy complications in the United States. Global public health crises increase the risk of these disorders, impact obstetric professionals that serve perinatal women, and introduce new challenges to accessing mental healthcare, particularly for economically marginalized perinatal women. Accordingly, the study purpose is to develop a taxonomy of mental healthcare access during public health crises for economically marginalized perinatal women.
source_label: Taxonomy of access to mental healthcare for economically marginalized women during a public health crisis: a qualitative study of obstetric professionals and perinatal women during the COVID-19 pandemic
